# LoopNet.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/loopnet-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/loopnet-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects commercial real estate listing data from LoopNet.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Code:** [`loopnet.py`](loopnet.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Listings](results/listings.json) · [Search](results/search.json)

## What it scrapes

- LoopNet search pages for finding commercial property listings
- LoopNet listing pages for property details, broker info, and images

## Functions

- `scrape_listings(urls)` → `List[LoopnetListing]`
- `scrape_search(search_url, max_pages=3)` → `SearchResult`

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import loopnet


async def main():
    listings = await loopnet.scrape_listings(
        urls=[
            "https://www.loopnet.com/Listing/2312-Abercorn-St-Savannah-GA/41217887/",
            "https://www.loopnet.com/Listing/1410-Dean-Forest-Rd-Savannah-GA/41166496/",
        ],
    )
    search = await loopnet.scrape_search(
        search_url="https://www.loopnet.com/search/commercial-real-estate/savannah-ga/for-sale/",
        max_pages=2,
    )


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields:

- **`LoopnetBroker`**: `name?`, `company?`, `phone?`, `profile_url?`
- **`LoopnetListing`**: `id?`, `name`, `url`, `description?`, `price?`, `address?`, `city?`, `state?`, `zip_code?`, `property_type?`, `property_subtype?`, `images`, `video_url?`, `broker?`, `details`
- **`LoopnetSearchResult`**: `id?`, `name?`, `url`, `address?`, `city?`, `state?`, `zip_code?`, `price?`, `property_type?`, `listing_type?`, `image?`, `data_points`
- **`SearchResult`**: `total_pages`, `data`

A field marked `?` can be `null`.

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`loopnet.py`](loopnet.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `unblocker` = `True`: Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker), its anti-bot bypass
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/loopnet-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_listing_scraping`, `test_search_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
